description: KESARVAL WATERFALL Kesarval Waterfall, also known as Kesarval Spring, is a beautiful natural attraction located near Verna village in South Goa, about 22 km from Panjim and close to the Zuari River. Surrounded by lush green forests and rocky hills, this waterfall is famous for its clear, mineral-rich spring water, which locals believe has therapeutic and healing properties for the skin and body. The name "Kesarval" is derived from the word “Kesar,” meaning eagle, as these birds were once seen nesting on the nearby cliffs. The water cascades down from the forested hill into a shallow pool, making it a refreshing spot for visitors, especially during the monsoon season (June to September) when the spring is at its full flow. The tranquil atmosphere, chirping birds, and cool breeze make Kesarval Waterfall a perfect getaway for nature lovers and those seeking peace away from Goa’s busy beaches. It’s easily accessible from Verna Industrial Estate and is a great place to relax, rejuvenate, and enjoy the natural beauty of South Goa. KESARVAL WATERFALL OVERVIEW Nestled in the serene landscapes of Goa, Kesarval Waterfall is an enchanting natural wonder that captivates visitors throughout the year. This hidden gem, often overshadowed by other popular tourist destinations in Goa, offers a refreshing escape into nature’s embrace. The cascading waters of Kesarval tumble from a height of about 30 meters, creating a melodious symphony that resonates through the lush greenery surrounding the falls. Located near the vibrant town of Verna, it serves as a perfect spot for nature lovers, adventure enthusiasts, and those looking to unwind in a tranquil setting. KESARVAL WATERFALL HISTORY Kesarval Waterfall has not just natural beauty but also a rich history. The area surrounding the waterfall is known for its natural springs, which the locals believe possess medicinal properties. Historically, the waterfall has been a significant site for the community, who have always revered it as a place of healing and rejuvenation. The name 'Kesarval' is derived from the Hindi word ‘kesar’ meaning saffron, attributed to the vibrant colors of the flora in the area, especially during the monsoon season when flowers bloom abundantly. Over the years, Kesarval has become a favored destination for both tourists and locals, known for its pristine beauty and tranquility. KESARVAL SPRING VERNA WATERFALL Kesarval Spring, also known as Kesarval Waterfall, is a hidden natural gem located near Verna village in South Goa, just off the Cortalim–Verna road. Surrounded by lush greenery and dense tropical forests, this scenic waterfall flows down rocky slopes, creating a soothing and refreshing atmosphere. The name “Kesarval” is derived from the word “Kesar,” meaning eagles, as the cliffs nearby were once home to many of these majestic birds. The spring is believed to have medicinal properties, and locals often visit to bathe in its mineral-rich waters, which are said to rejuvenate the skin and body. The site is especially popular during the monsoon season, when the water flows more vigorously and the surroundings turn vibrant green. Easily accessible from Margao, Vasco da Gama, and Panaji, Kesarval Spring offers a peaceful retreat for those seeking a break from Goa’s busy beaches — making it a perfect spot for nature lovers, photographers, and wellness seekers alike. VERNA WATERFALL Verna Waterfall, located in the serene village of Verna in South Goa, is a hidden natural gem surrounded by lush greenery and tranquil forest trails. The waterfall flows gently through the rocky terrain, creating a soothing atmosphere perfect for nature lovers and peace seekers. Unlike the crowded tourist spots, Verna Waterfall remains relatively untouched, offering visitors a refreshing escape into nature. The area around the falls is ideal for short hikes, photography, and quiet relaxation amidst the sounds of flowing water and chirping birds. Located close to the Kesarval Spring and just a short drive from Verna Industrial Estate and Cortalim Junction, the waterfall is easy to reach. It’s best visited during the monsoon or early winter months when the water flows more abundantly, revealing the true beauty of Goa’s hidden landscapes. Verna Waterfall is a must-visit for those seeking a peaceful, offbeat experience away from the busy Goan beaches. BEST TIME TO VISIT KESARVAL WATERFALL The best time to visit Kesarval Waterfall is during the monsoon season, which typically lasts from June to September. During this period, the waterfall is at its most magnificent, with increased water flow and vibrant greenery all around. It is advisable to visit the waterfall in the early morning or late afternoon to enjoy cooler temperatures and lesser crowds. The months of October to February also offer pleasant weather, making it an excellent time for trekking and picnicking; however, the waterfall may have reduced water flow during the dry months. Each season has its charm, and depending on your preference for water levels and activities, you can choose the perfect timing for your visit. CULTURAL AND LOCAL SIGNIFICANCE Kesarval Waterfall is not just a natural attraction but also carries cultural significance for the local communities. It is often associated with local folklore and serves as a gathering place for community celebrations and festivals. The waterfall symbolizes the natural bounty of Goa, reminding visitors of the region's rich cultural heritage and the importance of preserving natural ecosystems. Moreover, local artisans often showcase their crafts and paintings inspired by the beauty surrounding the waterfall, providing a platform for cultural exchange and support for local economies. Engaging with the local community during your visit can provide deeper insights into traditional rituals and the ecological importance of this stunning landscape. Where is Kesarval Waterfall located?

Kesarval Waterfall is located near Verna village in South Goa, along the Panjim–Margao highway. It is surrounded by lush greenery and natural rock formations, making it a popular spot for nature lovers.

How can I reach Kesarval Waterfall?

You can reach Kesarval Waterfall by road from Panjim (around 22 km) or Margao (about 15 km). It is easily accessible via the NH66 highway, and local taxis or scooters are convenient options for travelers.

What is the best time to visit Kesarval Waterfall?

The best time to visit Kesarval Waterfall is during the monsoon season, from June to September, when the waterfall is in full flow and the surrounding forest looks lush and vibrant.

Is swimming allowed at Kesarval Waterfall?

Yes, visitors often take a dip in the natural pool at Kesarval Waterfall. However, it is advisable to be cautious, especially during heavy rains, as the rocks can be slippery and the current strong.

Are there any entry fees for Kesarval Waterfall?

No, there are no entry fees for visiting Kesarval Waterfall. It is a public attraction open to all nature enthusiasts and travelers exploring South Goa.

What are the nearby attractions to Kesarval Waterfall?

Some nearby attractions to Kesarval Waterfall include Cansaulim Beach, Arossim Beach, Shree Mangueshi Temple, and the Rachol Fort and Seminary. These spots are within a short drive from the waterfall.

Are there food stalls or restaurants near Kesarval Waterfall?

There are small eateries and local restaurants near Kesarval Waterfall, especially along the Verna and Cortalim areas, where visitors can enjoy Goan snacks and refreshments.

Is Kesarval Waterfall suitable for family visits?

Yes, Kesarval Waterfall is a family-friendly destination. The serene environment and natural pool make it a perfect spot for picnics and short nature trips.

Can I visit Kesarval Waterfall during summer?

Kesarval Waterfall tends to dry up during the summer months, so it’s best to plan your visit during or right after the monsoon for the best experience.

Why is Kesarval Waterfall famous?

Kesarval Waterfall is famous for its natural beauty and for the mineral-rich spring water, which locals believe has healing properties. It’s a hidden gem that showcases Goa’s lush, untouched side beyond its beaches.

accordion_sections.title: Where is Kesarval Waterfall located?
accordion_sections.content: Kesarval Waterfall is located near Verna village in South Goa, along the Panjim–Margao highway. It is surrounded by lush greenery and natural rock formations, making it a popular spot for nature lovers.

accordion_sections.title: How can I reach Kesarval Waterfall?
accordion_sections.content: You can reach Kesarval Waterfall by road from Panjim (around 22 km) or Margao (about 15 km). It is easily accessible via the NH66 highway, and local taxis or scooters are convenient options for travelers.

accordion_sections.title: What is the best time to visit Kesarval Waterfall?
accordion_sections.content: The best time to visit Kesarval Waterfall is during the monsoon season, from June to September, when the waterfall is in full flow and the surrounding forest looks lush and vibrant.

accordion_sections.title: Is swimming allowed at Kesarval Waterfall?
accordion_sections.content: Yes, visitors often take a dip in the natural pool at Kesarval Waterfall. However, it is advisable to be cautious, especially during heavy rains, as the rocks can be slippery and the current strong.

accordion_sections.title: Are there any entry fees for Kesarval Waterfall?
accordion_sections.content: No, there are no entry fees for visiting Kesarval Waterfall. It is a public attraction open to all nature enthusiasts and travelers exploring South Goa.

accordion_sections.title: What are the nearby attractions to Kesarval Waterfall?
accordion_sections.content: Some nearby attractions to Kesarval Waterfall include Cansaulim Beach, Arossim Beach, Shree Mangueshi Temple, and the Rachol Fort and Seminary. These spots are within a short drive from the waterfall.

accordion_sections.title: Are there food stalls or restaurants near Kesarval Waterfall?
accordion_sections.content: There are small eateries and local restaurants near Kesarval Waterfall, especially along the Verna and Cortalim areas, where visitors can enjoy Goan snacks and refreshments.

accordion_sections.title: Is Kesarval Waterfall suitable for family visits?
accordion_sections.content: Yes, Kesarval Waterfall is a family-friendly destination. The serene environment and natural pool make it a perfect spot for picnics and short nature trips.

accordion_sections.title: Can I visit Kesarval Waterfall during summer?
accordion_sections.content: Kesarval Waterfall tends to dry up during the summer months, so it’s best to plan your visit during or right after the monsoon for the best experience.

accordion_sections.title: Why is Kesarval Waterfall famous?
accordion_sections.content: Kesarval Waterfall is famous for its natural beauty and for the mineral-rich spring water, which locals believe has healing properties. It’s a hidden gem that showcases Goa’s lush, untouched side beyond its beaches.

guidelines: Safety First: Always check the weather conditions before visiting Kesarval Waterfall. Heavy rains can increase water flow and create hazardous conditions. Make sure to wear appropriate footwear to prevent slipping on wet rocks.

Respect Local Customs: When visiting the waterfall, be mindful of the surroundings and local culture. Avoid littering and take all your belongings with you. If you encounter locals, greet them respectfully and inquire about any customs or guidelines they may have regarding the area.

Timing Your Visit: The best time to visit Kesarval Waterfall is during the monsoon season (June to September) when the waterfall is at its fullest. However, be cautious as it can get crowded during weekends and holidays. Plan your visit early in the morning or on weekdays for a more peaceful experience.

Swimming Caution: While swimming in the pools near the waterfall can be refreshing, be cautious of strong currents and sudden depths. Always swim with a buddy and never venture too close to the waterfall itself, as it can be dangerous.

Bring Essentials: Pack essentials like water, sunscreen, insect repellent, and snacks. A waterproof bag for your belongings can also be helpful, as you may encounter splashes or rain during your visit.

Photography Considerations: If you're interested in capturing the beauty of Kesarval Waterfall, bring a waterproof camera or use a protective case for your smartphone. Be respectful of other visitors while taking photos, and avoid blocking pathways to ensure everyone can enjoy the view.
